Questions.content: What is the total time spent on both activities combined, and how does this TG ensure the correct calculation of the total time?

What is the rationale for having a dependency from "CrosswordPuzzleTime" to "SudokuPuzzleTime" in the order section, when they can be calculated independently and then summed up directly? This might suggest an unnecessary sequential processing.

Answers.content:
The total time spent on both activities combined can be calculated by summing the time spent on crossword puzzles and sudoku puzzles.

Given:
- Time per crossword puzzle: 10 minutes
- Number of crossword puzzles solved: 3
- Time per sudoku puzzle: 5 minutes
- Number of sudoku puzzles solved: 8

First, calculate the total time spent on crossword puzzles:
\[ \text{Total time on crossword puzzles} = 10 \, \text{minutes/puzzle} \times 3 \, \text{puzzles} = 30 \, \text{minutes} \]

Next, calculate the total time spent on sudoku puzzles:
\[ \text{Total time on sudoku puzzles} = 5 \, \text{minutes/puzzle} \times 8 \, \text{puzzles} = 40 \, \text{minutes} \]

Finally, add the two totals to find the combined total time spent:
\[ \text{Total time spent} = 30 \, \text{minutes} + 40 \, \text{minutes} = 70 \, \text{minutes} \]

The TG ensures the correct calculation of the total time by sequentially calculating and combining the times for each type of puzzle before summing them up. The orders in the TG are structured to first calculate the time spent on crossword puzzles (CrosswordPuzzleTime), then the time spent on sudoku puzzles (SudokuPuzzleTime), and finally combine these values to get the total time spent (TotalTimeSpent).
